### Prerequisite edges (listed separately)

**P0-1 payoff → autopay_miss_late_fee_ground** (value_input, gate balance; source "any late payment fee on the card that was billed contrary to this charter must first be reversed").
- Entailment basis: blocked side — payoff_balance doc "A charge billed in breach of the charter, the kind whose proper ground of reversal is bank error, is not owed; an amount owed that still contains such a charge is not a figure on which the credit can properly be sized."; depended-on rules — the six autopay-miss docs (M1–M10), which declare the recent late fee "a fee the bank billed contrary to the card charter, to be taken back in full on the bank error ground"; records — late_payment fee 32.00 on 2026-09-12, autopay statement_balance, source active with negative_since 2026-09-13 > due 2026-09-11, no payment on 2026-09-11.
- Findability: the record's own words ("late_payment" fee, autopay) reach `doc_card_late_fee_under_examination_16022c4d`, `doc_card_autopay_miss_ground_determination_930a3b49` (`KB_search("late payment fee autopay")`).
- Strength: hard in both — on the triggered branch.
- Stated anywhere as a condition? No document names the late fee or autopay in connection with a points credit; the depended-on docs do not restate the payoff principle. But the blocked-side sentence states a sizing gate in abstract words (explicitness X0-1) and widens the class of charges (D1).

**P0-2 payoff → autopay_source_restoration** (state_gate; source "when the PCB checking account named as the card's autopay source is overdrawn, the points needed to restore it must first be deposited").
- Entailment basis: blocked side — points_pool doc "The pool a statement credit draws on is the card's points net of every other redemption that this charter requires in the same circumstance … and the count is taken from the ledger once no such redemption remains outstanding."; depended-on rule — restoration doc trigger S1–S2; records — card autopay source df4449dd, ledger −64.18.
- Findability: "overdrawn"/"below zero"/"autopay source" reach the restoration doc (`KB_search("checking account overdrawn autopay rewards")` → rank 1).
- Strength: hard in both.
- Stated? The timing half ("once no such redemption remains outstanding") is stated outright in abstract form; the identity of the redemption is derived (X0-2). The restoration doc carries only its own trigger, not the payoff principle.

### Differences

**D1 — widened prerequisite class (addition in untriggered branches).**
- Source: `card_ext_rewards_balance_payoff.rule` — "any **late payment fee** on the card that was billed contrary to this charter must first be reversed, so that the balance the points pay reflects only what the cardholder owes"; `prerequisite[0].condition` — "Every **late payment fee** on the card that was billed contrary to the charter has been reversed before the rewards statement credit is sized."
- KB: `doc_card_payoff_balance_and_covering_points_5cd9bed6`, "The amount to be paid" — "A **charge** billed in breach of the charter, the kind whose proper ground of reversal is bank error, is not owed; an amount owed that still contains such a charge is not a figure on which the credit can properly be sized."
- Root cause: the rendering generalises the object from late payment fees to every bank-error charge. Other bank-error charges exist in the same corpus: "Interest billed in error … is reversed on the bank error ground" (`doc_card_interest_charges_a3b97463`), "an annual fee billed although the first-year waiver … ruled it out" (`doc_card_fee_reversals_38c67276`).
- Consequence in an untriggered branch: a card carrying, say, interest billed at a rate the charter does not allow, but no bad late fee, is sized by the source on current_balance as it stands; by the KB that balance "is not a figure on which the credit can properly be sized" — a gate the source does not impose (and no task tool of this difficulty reverses interest).
- This task's scored values are unaffected (the only bank-error charge on the card is the late fee).

- **N1 (base section of `blueprint/products/card.yaml`, `card_evt_payments`)**: the rule text says the minimum is the greater of the floor and "minimum_payment_pct percent of the new statement balance plus the interest and fees billed on that statement", while the same policy's `formula.minimum_due` is `min(max(minimum_payment_floor, round(last_statement_balance * minimum_payment_pct / 100, 2)), last_statement_balance)` — no interest or fees. The two disagree whenever a statement bills interest or fees. The KB follows the rule text (`doc_card_payment_crediting_and_minimum_due_174a3816`: "the tier's percentage of the new statement balance with the interest and fees billed on that statement added to it"), and so do the seeded records (task 1: 1 % × 343.02 + 95.00 fee = 98.43 = `minimum_payment_due`). Nature: internal inconsistency of a base policy (rule vs formula). Scored values moved: none — `minimum_payment_due` is read from records in both tasks, and task 0's instruction (`statement_balance`) does not compare against it.

## explicitness

Hop marks carried from the blind answer: H1 derived (with note), H2 read off (order), H3/H4 derived.

**X0-1 — stated sizing gate on the blocked side.** `doc_card_payoff_balance_and_covering_points_5cd9bed6`, "The amount to be paid": "an amount owed that still contains such a charge is not a figure on which the credit can properly be sized." The preceding clauses ("That figure stands only for sums the cardholder genuinely owes …"; "A charge billed in breach of the charter … is not owed") already carry the principle; this clause adds the gate itself ("still contains" → the credit waits until the charge is gone). It names neither late fees nor the reversal, so which charge qualifies is still derived. Semantics carried: P0-1 must be resolved before the credit is sized. Severity: low.

**X0-2 — stated order between redemptions (abstract gating clause).** `doc_card_payoff_points_pool_66186a8b`, "What the pool excludes": "The pool a statement credit draws on is the card's points net of every other redemption that this charter requires in the same circumstance, that is, on a cardholder's request to spend points against the card's debt. Points that the charter sends somewhere else in that circumstance never form part of the pool, and the count is taken from the ledger once no such redemption remains outstanding." The sentence tells the reader, without any combination, that on a payoff request another required redemption may exist and that the credit's count waits until it is done ("once no such redemption remains outstanding"). Only the identity of that redemption (the restoring deposit) has to be found. Semantics carried: P0-2 before P0. Blind hop H2 was marked read off (order) on this sentence.

**X0-3 — templated wording across documents.**
- `doc_card_rewards_statement_credit_payoff_2334d1a1`: "This page is the entry point for that use of points." / `doc_card_closing_points_cash_out_fbff4167`: "This page is the entry point for that closing cash-out."
- `doc_card_autopay_source_restoration_redemption_642f2c1b` "How it is recorded": "The redemption is recorded on the card alone: the card's redemption entry identifies the checking account that receives the money and states the cash delivered. This card rule does not itself post the corresponding entry on the checking account's own ledger, and nothing in this rule reads that ledger entry or waits for it." / `doc_card_closing_points_cash_out_fbff4167` "How it is recorded": "The cash-out is recorded on the card only: the card's redemption entry identifies the receiving checking account and states the cash value paid. This card rule does not post the counterpart entry on the checking account's own ledger, and nothing in the rule depends on that entry or waits for it to appear." — same sentence frame, same heading, word-level substitutions only; both are also near-verbatim renderings of the charter sentence "the matching entry on the checking account's own ledger is not posted by this card policy, and nothing in this policy reads or waits for it".

**Observations (not counted RED): close, structure-preserving paraphrases of charter sentences** — restoration doc "since an account below zero cannot fund the automatic payment that pays the card" (charter: "because an overdrawn source cannot fund the autopay that pays the card"); payoff_checking_relationship "Such an account can take any points beyond the card's debt at a later time … never pushed into a credit balance" (charter: "which can receive any points beyond the balance later … so the card is not pushed into a credit balance"); autopay_miss determination "neither used up nor looked at" (charter: "neither used nor consulted"); redemption_and_forfeiture quotes the retired clause verbatim ("a deposit to a PCB checking or savings account of the same customer"), which serves as an identifier of the retired text.

Checked and not RED:
- Titles/openings of this task's documents name general subjects ("When a Missed Autopay Debit Is the Bank's Error", "Rewards Deposits Restoring an Overdrawn Autopay Account", "Points Available to a Statement Credit" …); none restates the caller's request.
- `doc_card_autopay_source_restoration_redemption_642f2c1b` "It applies when a cardholder seeks to put rewards points toward what a card owes at a time when the PCB checking account … is overdrawn" is the restoration policy's own trigger (source S1), not a restatement of the payoff's principle; it makes H2's identification one search away but states no order.
- No example, FAQ or contrast walks from the payoff to the late fee or the restoration; no document names the payoff tool together with another task tool.
- Depended-on documents are reachable through the records' own words (late payment fee, autopay, overdrawn/below zero).

**KB-EXPLICIT: RED** (task 0) — X0-1, X0-2, X0-3.
